podcast.title: Manslaughter of Marie Trintignant - July/August 2003
podcast.body: In July 2003, during an argument over infidelity with his girlfriend, French actress Marie Trintignant, Cantat reportedly hit her 19 times, causing irreversible brain damage. She fell into a coma and died on August 1, 2003, leading to a significant public outcry in France, including an arson attack on his house. "But then in July 2003, he was in a hotel room with his girlfriend, a French actress named Marie Trignan, and things went horribly, horribly wrong. There was an argument over infidelity. She had apparently received a love text from her ex-husband. And that's when Bertrand apparently hit her 19 times, knocking her unconscious. Then he tucked her into bed. She suffered irreversible brain damage, went into a coma, and died on August 1, 2003."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Conviction and Early Release - 2004/2007
podcast.body: In March 2004, Cantat was found guilty of manslaughter and sentenced to eight years in a Lithuanian prison. He was released early on October 17, 2007, having served approximately three and a half years for the death of his girlfriend. "In March of 2004, Kentatz was found guilty and sentenced to eight years in a lift-to-winning prison for manslaughter. By the way, Bertrand Kentatz was released early from jail. He got out on October 17, 2007, serving about three and a half years for the manslaughter of his actress girlfriend."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Frontman of Noir Désir
podcast.body: Bertrand Cantat was the frontman for the French band Noir Désir. "Bertrand Kentatz was a French rock star. He was the frontman for a band called Noire Dezier, Black Desire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Political Activism in the 1990s
podcast.body: In the 1990s, Cantat was highly prominent in France due to his left-wing views on issues like Iraq, globalization, and the environment. "Back in the 90s, Bertrand was huge in France. He was all over the news with his left wing views about Iraq and globalization and the environment."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Homicide of Marie Trintignant (2003)
xref.body: In 2003, during an affair in Vilnius, Lithuania, frontman Bertrand Cantat got into a fight with French actress Marie Trintignant over a text message from her husband. Cantat admitted to slapping her four times before putting her to bed, but she was dying. She died a few days later after emergency surgery in France; a post-mortem revealed 19 blows to the head, likely from large rings Cantat was wearing, akin to brass knuckles. "Seven hours later, Marie was in the emergency ward, Contat admitted to slapping Marie four times before he put her to bed."
